summary: Intermittent presigned artifact truncation + 502s over ExpressRoute: HTTP/2 connection pooling + MTU clamp
description:
Issue summary:
FinTechWorks reports intermittent failures when Redwood private agents fetch large presigned model artifacts (50–200MB) from S3-backed storage. Failures manifest as: (a) partial file writes (artifact truncated by a few KB to several MB) followed by checksum mismatch on agent side, (b) transient 502/504 errors surfaced to the application during model pulls, and (c) sporadic long-lived gRPC stream resets after artifact fetch attempts succeed but streaming later fails.

Impact:
- Several worker nodes repeatedly fail model startup leading to reduced throughput and degraded SLAs for production features.
- Affected traffic localized to FinTechWorks EU private deployment and coincides with scheduled business-hours traffic spikes.

Environment:
- Private deployment (VPC) peered to Redwood control plane via ExpressRoute/partner link.
- Agents run on customer-managed subnet with NAT egress through corporate edge appliance that performs HTTP/2 multiplexing and connection pooling to a corporate proxy.
- Customer reports corporate edge enforces TCP MSS clamp (MSS reduced to 1200) and an SD-WAN vendor applies per-flow HTTP/2 connection coalescing.

Steps to reproduce (customer provided):
1) Trigger a model update that causes agents to download artifact with size ~120MB via presigned URL.
2) Observe agent download attempt in logs; occasionally download completes but saved file size < expected and checksum mismatch occurs.
3) Agent retries; sometimes subsequent attempt succeeds, sometimes fails with HTTP 502 from edge proxy.

Observed behavior / logs (excerpts):
- Agent log (successful partial + checksum): "GET https://s3.internal-presigned/... 200 OK, bytes_received=118,742,912 expected=120,056,345 checksum mismatch"
- Edge proxy log: "upstream response 502: connection reset after transfer completion, stream_id=23"
- tcpdump (customer): repeated TCP retransmits after TLS ServerHello; final segment size larger than path MTU and blackholed until retransmit with smaller MSS.

Preliminary hypothesis:
- Combination of an enforced MSS/TCP MSS clamp at the customer edge + HTTP/2 connection pooling across multiple upstream destinations appears to cause an MTU/multipart fragmentation blackhole for large TLS records. When the presigned download uses persistent HTTP/2 connection that gets pooled across flows, some TLS record fragmentation crosses the MSS boundary and is lost by a middlebox. The agent perceives truncated body and reports checksum mismatch; in some cases the proxy or upstream returns 502.

Why different from prior tickets:
- Existing support cases typically call out ALPN/SNI rewrites, header injection, or SNI stripping. This case is distinct because the customer has a combination of aggressive HTTP/2 pooling (coalescing unrelated host flows onto shared TCP/TLS sessions) and an SD-WAN MSS clamp producing fragmentation that selectively affects large presigned downloads, not general small control-plane calls.

Immediate customer workaround requested:
- Temporarily disable HTTP/2 pooling / connection coalescing on corporate edge for flows to Redwood S3 endpoints OR disable MSS clamp on path for agent subnets. Customer cannot change both quickly; asked for guidance which is lower-risk.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Support (Aisha): Acknowledged ticket to customer, requested packet captures and edge proxy config dump. Asked for timestamped agent log and expected file size.

2026-03-11 - Customer (FinTechWorks - network ops): Uploaded tcpdump (pcap) and edge-proxy config snippet. Noted MSS clamp applied by SD-WAN controller to 1200 bytes and HTTP/2 pooled tunnels enabled. Reported issue frequency ~4% of downloads during peak window.

2026-03-12 - SRE (Luca): Reproduced locally by configuring a lab proxy to clamp MSS and enable HTTP/2 connection coalescing; observed truncated body on large downloads when server-side emitted large TLS record crossing MSS. Filed hypothesis in ticket and linked reproducer. Asked for temporary mitigation to disable pooling for Redwood endpoints.

2026-03-13 - Customer: Disabled HTTP/2 pooling for a 1-hour window (as requested) and reported immediate drop in failure rate to 0.2% during the test window. Confirmed MSS clamp still in place. Asked for permanent mitigation suggestions.

2026-03-14 - Support (Luca): Proposed two remediation paths: 1) request customer change to avoid pooling or lift MSS clamp; 2) on Redwood side, serve presigned downloads with smaller TLS record sizes (split writes) as a compatibility workaround. Opened INT-20488 to evaluate artifact-serving server-side chunking and checkout of HTTP/2 behaviour.
2026-03-14 - Customer: Prefers server-side mitigation while they schedule change control for SD-WAN. Asked for ETA on Redwood-side fix and possible performance impacts.
investigation_notes:
Reproducer: Created a lab proxy that enforces MSS=1200 and enables http2 coalescing (multiplexing unrelated Host headers on same connection). Ran presigned download from S3-compatible backend. Observed that when server issues TLS record >1200 (e.g., a 16KB TLS record), the middlebox drops fragments and TCP retransmit behavior results in truncated read in the application layer. When same download is performed over non-pooled connection or with MSS large enough, no truncation. Additional observations: TLS-level fragmentation makes behavior non-deterministic and dependent on server-side write sizes and connection reuse timing.

Heap of evidence: pcap, agent logs, edge-proxy config. Linked INT ticket created to evaluate server-side TLS write-size control and whether we can force smaller TLS record sizes for artifact responses or switch to chunked-range requests to avoid large contiguous TLS records.

Related artifacts: pcap stored in FinTechWorks-share (link redacted), reproducer script in internal sandbox repo (gh:infra/reproducers#1287).
resolution:
Workaround implemented: Customer temporarily disabled http2 connection pooling for Redwood S3 endpoints; failures dropped to near-zero.
Planned fixes: INT-20488 opened to prototype server-side mitigation (split large artifact responses into smaller TLS writes / enable chunked-range transfers) with target PR in two sprints. Provided customer runbook steps for permanent network change: 1) exempt agent subnets from MSS clamp or 2) disable HTTP/2 pooling for flows to Redwood artifact domains, with suggested firewall rules and rationale.
Follow-ups: After INT-20488 reproducer completes, will schedule rollout of server-side compatibility mode behind a feature flag and notify FinTechWorks for canary. Ticket remains open until server-side mitigations are validated or customer confirms network change.
